IPRoyal is a sensible NetNut replacement for small and mid-size teams: you can start with a single gigabyte, residential traffic never expires, SOCKS5 is supported, and sticky sessions run up to seven days, which suits account work NetNut customers ran on its static IPs. It also sells ISP proxies, the product NetNut was best known for. Teams that used NetNut at enterprise volume may prefer a larger pool, but for most former customers IPRoyal is a low-risk, well-documented place to land.

Most people searching IPRoyal vs NetNut in 2026 are former NetNut customers looking for somewhere to move. NetNut's domains were seized by the FBI in July 2026 after Google linked its residential network to the Popa botnet, so this page compares IPRoyal with what NetNut used to offer and explains how to migrate. IPRoyal's non-expiring traffic, long sticky sessions and published consent documentation make it one of the easier landing spots for small and mid-size NetNut users.
What happened to NetNut?

On July 2, 2026, the FBI, working with IRS Criminal Investigation, Google, Lumen and the Shadowserver Foundation, seized hundreds of domains tied to NetNut, the residential proxy service owned by Nasdaq-listed Alarum Technologies. Google's Threat Intelligence Group said NetNut's exit-node pool overlapped with Popa, a botnet it estimated at about two million consumer devices, many of them smart TVs and streaming boxes. Alarum disputes the botnet label and said it would cooperate with law enforcement, but netnut.com and, within days, netnut.io displayed federal seizure notices. As of October 2026 the service is not something you can responsibly buy or rely on.

How to migrate from NetNut to IPRoyal

1. Export your NetNut usage history and list the countries, cities and session types you actually used, so you can map them to IPRoyal's targeting (country, state and city (ISP selection needs verification)).

2. Test before you commit. IPRoyal's testing option: no general free trial; Enterprise trial for verified companies. Run your real targets for a day on the smallest purchase before moving production traffic.

Where IPRoyal fits best
General web scraping: strong fit. Why: solid success rates and non-expiring traffic for bursty crawls.
SERP and rank tracking: workable. Why: it works, but it has no dedicated SERP product.
Social media and multi-account management: strong fit. Why: 7-day sticky sessions keep one IP on one account.
E-commerce price and stock monitoring: strong fit. Why: city targeting with pay-only-for-what-you-use traffic.
Ad verification and geo-testing: workable. Why: decent coverage but no ASN or carrier targeting on standard accounts.
Tight budgets: strong fit. Why: small entry purchases and traffic that never expires.
Protocols and sessions

IPRoyal supports HTTP, HTTPS, SOCKS5 and offers rotating or sticky sessions from 1 second up to 7 days. Targeting covers country, state and city (ISP selection needs verification) across 195 countries. Like NetNut's residential gateway, it works through a single backconnect endpoint with location and session options passed in the username, plus IP whitelisting.
How to vet a residential proxy provider after NetNut

NetNut's customers did not choose to route traffic through a botnet; they bought what looked like a standard enterprise service. The lesson is to check sourcing before you buy, not after. Whichever provider replaces NetNut for you, IPRoyal included, run through these checks:
How are residential IPs sourced? Look for an opt-in SDK or app programme with clear user
consent and compensation, and ask which partner apps are involved.
Does the provider publish an ethics or sourcing policy, and has it been audited or certified (for
example AppEsteem or ISO 27001)?
What KYC does the provider apply to customers, and which target categories are restricted?
Strict onboarding is a good sign, not an inconvenience.
How does it handle abuse reports, and is there a named legal entity and jurisdiction behind the
service?
Can you get contractual assurances, such as a data-processing agreement, if your compliance
team needs them?
Bottom line

NetNut is no longer a provider you can plan around, so the real decision is which network replaces it.
